title: "Identity and Authorization"
execute:

## Production identity flow

Apache performs LDAP authentication before proxying `/ppsv-app/`. At virtual
host scope it removes all client-controlled identity headers, including
`X-Remote-User`, name, email, group, and phone variants. Inside the protected
location it injects values obtained from the successful LDAP request:

- `X-Remote-User` from `REMOTE_USER`;
- `X-Remote-Name` from the LDAP display name;
- `X-Remote-Email` from the LDAP mail attribute;
- `X-Remote-Group` from the configured organizational attribute; and
- `X-Remote-Phone` from the LDAP telephone attribute.

The application accepts that trusted proxy identity only when `AUTH_MODE=ldap`.
There is no production identity through query parameters, cookies, form fields,
local passwords, or default credentials. If Apache does not provide a valid
authenticated username, the application fails closed.

Usernames are normalized case-insensitively. LDAP profile values and their
verification flags are synchronized at login, and the application records the
last login. A missing LDAP name or email may be supplied in a request, but is
marked unverified and is not promoted to a trusted mail identity.

## Fixed role allowlist

Roles are derived from this version-controlled allowlist on every security
decision. A role value supplied by a UI event, database row, or header is not
trusted.

| Role | Usernames |
|---|---|
| `admin` | `yeroslaviz`, `basquin` |
| `technician` | `grzejszc`, `pleyer`, `valer`, `wehner`, `yaoxiao`, `piroddi` |
| `user` | Every other active LDAP user |

The `b_profa` group is used only for the project-pool ACL. Membership never
grants technician or administrator privileges in the application. There is no
role editor.

## Permission matrix

Every permission below is enforced in server handlers and backend lifecycle or
repository functions. Hiding a button is only a usability feature.

| Action | User | Technician | Admin |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Submit a request or inquiry | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| View own request, including closed | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| View all requests | No | Yes | Yes |
| Edit own non-closed request | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Edit another user's non-archived request | No | Yes | Yes |
| Add an input file to own non-closed request | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Add input/results to any non-archived request | No | Yes | Yes |
| Change status and add history note | No | Yes | Yes |
| Assign a technician or admin | No | Yes | Yes |
| Download an authorized file or PDF | Own only | Yes | Yes |
| See own request's ticket state | Own only | Yes | Yes |
| See the global delivery log | No | Yes | Yes |
| View an archived request by direct ID | No | No | Yes |
| Archive a request | No | No | Yes |
| Archive a file | No | No | Yes |
| View/manage user activation | No | No | Yes |
| Manually retry a failed outbox item | No | No | Yes |

There is no permanent purge action in v1. A technician cannot delete or
archive requests or files. A `Closed` owner request remains readable but cannot
be edited or receive owner uploads. Once an administrator archives a request,
it is hidden from owners and technicians even when they try a direct request
ID; administrators can still view it from the archived listing.

## Account activation

The admin directory displays normalized username, derived role, LDAP profile,
active state, and last login. An admin may activate or deactivate a non-admin
account. Activation is an additional gate; it never changes the user's derived
role. The fixed administrator role is not editable through the application.

When investigating an access report, check both the allowlist-derived role and
the active flag. Do not add a person to `b_profa` as a substitute for an
application role change.

## Test mode

`AUTH_MODE=test` exists only for automated tests and isolated local
development. It can use `PPSV_TEST_USER`, `PPSV_TEST_NAME`, and
`PPSV_TEST_EMAIL`; the username still receives its role from the same
allowlist. Production provisioning requires `AUTH_MODE=ldap`.

Never switch a public VM to test mode for maintenance. Diagnose the Apache/LDAP
path instead, and keep port 3838 loopback-only.

## Spoof-resistance acceptance

Before handoff, prove all of the following:

1. An unauthenticated HTTPS request containing `X-Remote-User: forged-admin`
   receives an LDAP challenge rather than administrator access.
2. An authenticated request with that same forged header is represented as the
   real LDAP user, because Apache removed and replaced the header.
3. Query strings and cookies cannot select another identity.
4. Direct network access to port 3838 is unavailable off-host.
5. A forged Shiny event or direct request ID is rejected by backend
   authorization when the record belongs to another user.

`scripts/verify_deployment.sh --netrc FILE` automates the first two HTTP checks
when given a temporary mode-`0600` netrc. Backend authorization cases are also
covered by the automated test suite.
